Retail Radar
Jul 29 – Momentum Unwind, Cutting Tech Losses
Retail Trading Activity Overview
Sentiment deteriorated further this week as retail flows meaningfully weakened, reaching their 0.8%ile vs 1y history; this time, retail investors aggressively pulled out of single names (3.2%ile, with 4 consecutive days of single-stock selling, Figure 10Retail Investor DailyPurchase byStocks andETFs), while only modestly adding exposure to ETFs (1.6%ile).
. Within ETFs, Tech saw significant outflows—the second-largest on record, behind only the week ending June 10th, Figure 5Wekly Outfows TechEFs werthcond igheston rcd, driven primarily by SOXL (-1.2z, Figure 6Cumlative RlImbance iSOXL). Retail investors also cut exposure to crypto ETFs, led by BITO (-4.9z).
Single-stock selling was overwhelmingly concentrated in Tech. Hardware names took the brunt of the selling, posting their largest weekly selling on record, Figure 7Wekly Outfows TechHardwe &Equipment sockwer thigson recd. SNDK was the biggest driver (-3.2z), followed by AAPL. In broader Semis, MU moved into the most-sold list among retail investors—just a few weeks after consistently featuring alongside SNDK among their favorites, Figure 8Memory Stcks:Cumlative RlNtBough. In line with this, our Crowding analysis that captures broader market positioning quantifies the sharp Semis de-crowding, down to the 91.8%ile from the 99%ile, see report and report, Figure 11Semis voftware Coding. In contrast, the Mag 7 + SPCX saw positive flows overall: NVDA, GOOGL, SPCX and TSLA were amongst the top 5 this week, alongside SKHY. Internationally, Korea has has undergone an intense period of de-leveraging since mid-June, with the positioning setup now appearing attractive on balance according to our analysts, see report.
The sharp deterioration in retail YTD P&L (Figure 9Retail Investor Singletocks P&L) may help explain why retail investors have been quick to cut Tech exposure as the Semis-led Momentum Unwind has weighed on portfolios (see Factor Crowdings and Rotations).
. As we head into peak-Earnings, investors are focusing on the major announcements slated for this week. Retail participation has been limited so far, underscoring a deterioration in sentiment, see Single Stock Stories with Elevated Retail Activity:
• Retail investors trimmed META, MSFT and QCOM on Wednesday before their announcements (-0.6z, 0.8z, and -0.2z, respectively). MSFT’s Cloud unit posted a larger-than-expected increase in sales at +43% y/y, with shares rising \~3% in post-market trading. Capex increased +70% y/y to \$41B during the quarter. META narrowed its 2026 capex guidance to \$130-145B, lifting the low-end from \$125B. Revenue for the quarter came in line with expectations, but next quarter’s outlook was lackluster. Shares fell as much as \~10% in post-market trading after the results were published. QCOM’s earnings missed expectations, but top line was better than expected. Additionally, the company expects non-handset revenue growth to accelerate to 60% in fiscal year 2027, as it tries to reduce its dependence on phones with a new push into the data center market.

AAPL also reports tomorrow, with price elasticity the key watchpoint after \~20% average price hikes across iPads and Macs—moves that have also lifted expectations for iPhone 18 pricing. While investors debate near-term consumer pushback amid higher memory costs, our analysts see multiple offsets that should leave revenue and earnings more resilient than feared (link).
Factor Crowdings and Rotations
. Amid weakening retail sentiment, a Momentum Unwind, and the recent market drawdown, we provide a few additional observations on investor positioning:
. (1) Crowding remains high across higher-risk segments (e.g., Low Quality at 94.8%ile and Speculative Growth at 98.0%ile), with Value also elevated (88.7%ile);
• (2) Momentum’s Beta exposure is high, and Momentum–Beta correlations have declined from extremes during this unwind; and
• (3) Implied stock correlations increased over the past week from historically low levels (COR3M <Index>), even as peak-Earnings season typically coincides with lower stock correlations. In many risk-model frameworks, higher implied correlations translate into higher implied betas and higher portfolio risk estimates, which lead systematic/quant portfolios to reduce net exposure as volatility targets and risk constraints bind.
• In combination with month-end Momentum rebalancing, these conditions are consistent with the elevated volatility observed in Momentum and higher-risk factors this week.

Retail Trading Activity in Numbers for the Week: Jul 23 to Jul 29
. Retail flows were \$2.2B this week, well below the 12-month average of \$6.8B/week. Retail investors continued to favor ETFs (+\$3.7B) over Single Stocks (-\$1.4B).
Outside of Broad Based Large Cap Equity ETFs (+\$1.5B), retail ETF buying was influenced by Equity Style Dividend (+\$261M), Equity Style Call/Put writing (+206M), Fixed Income – Multi Sector (+\$172M), and Equity Broad Based Multi Cap (+\$166M).
• This week, in line with prior weeks, retail investors continued to buy AI datacenters and electrification (JPAMAIDE), Mag 7, Top 30 AI/Datacenter Beneficiaries, Growth, along with AI Software/Product/Monetization, and OBBBA Immediate Expensing Beneficiaries, see Figure 4,Retail Sngetock AivtybThems.
. Activity in Mag7 this week: Retail investors bought NVDA (+\$601M), GOOGL/GOOG (+\$377M), TSLA (+\$121M), MSFT (+\$33M) and sold AMZN (-\$22M), META (-\$26M) and AAPL (-\$169M).
Outside of Mag7, retail investors favored Communications (+\$177M) and were net sellers of Tech (-\$2.2B), Industrials (-\$232M), Cons. Disc. (-\$200M) and Health Care (-\$176M).

Single Stock Stories with Elevated Retail Activity
Hedge Funds vs. Retail: High Short Interest Meme Stocks
DBGI (\$0.4M bought last week, 0.3z, Figure 19Retail Acvtyin DBGI): The company expanded its secured U.S. program by 32% to \$165M, driven by the addition of new apparel and footwear categories. Retail interest has been strong, with net purchases totaling \$70M since May 2026, amid moderate short interest of \~14% of float, up 10% over the same period.
INFQ (\$0.2M sold last week, -0.7z, Figure 20Retail Acvtyin INFQ): The company has undergone a series of management changes and secured three Genesis Mission projects from the U.S. Department of Energy focused on AI-optimized quantum circuit design for nuclear applications. The stock has been on retail investors’ radar, with net purchases totaling \$120M since March 2026, alongside elevated short interest of \~16% of float.
JOBY (\$13.4M bought last week, -0.0z, Figure 21Retail Acvtyin JOBY): The company signed a binding agreement with Virgin Atlantic, naming it Joby’s exclusive airline partner for air taxi services in the UK. Retail investors have purchased \$400M year-to-date, against a backdrop of high short interest of \~18% of float, which has increased by 8% over the same period.
Earnings Stories
. AAPL (\$18.6M sold on 7/29, -0.0z, Figure 22Retail Imbncei APL): Apple reports earnings tomorrow AMC, with price elasticity of demand the biggest watchpoint for the company across its key hardware product lines following the announcement of a \~20% price increase on average across iPads and Macs, which also raised expectations for the magnitude of price increases likely to be enacted in conjunction with the launch of iPhone 18. However, even as short-term consumer responses to the unprecedented price increases, precipitated by the rise in memory costs, are being debated by investors, our analysts believe there are several drivers to lead the revenue and earnings outcomes to be much more favorable than currently feared by investors (link).
• AMZN (\$9.8M bought on 7/29, -0.1z, Figure 24Retail Imbncei AMZN): Amazon reports tomorrow AMC, with our analysts expecting AWS growth acceleration of low-mid 30%’s, higher capex guidance and retail margin expansion (link).
• MSFT (\$23.4M bought on 7/29, -0.2z, Figure 26Retail Imbncei MSFT): Microsoft’s Cloud unit posted a larger-than-expected increase in sales at +43% y/y, with shares rising \~3% in post-market trading. Capex increased +70% y/y to \$41B during the quarter.
META (\$2.2M sold on 7/29, -0.4z, Figure 28Retail Imbncei META): Meta narrowed its 2026 capex guidance to \$130-145B, lifting the low-end from \$125B. Revenue for the quarter came in line with expectations, but next quarter’s outlook was lackluster. Shares fell as much as \~10% in post-market trading after the results were published.
QCOM (\$6.8M sold on 7/29, -0.6z, Figure 30Retail Imbncei QCOM): Qualcomm’s earnings missed expectations, but top line was better than expected. Additionally, the company expects non-handset revenue growth to accelerate to 60% in fiscal year 2027, as it tries to reduce its dependence on phones with a new push into the data center market.
V (\$2.9M sold on 7/29, -0.2z, Figure 32Retail Imbncei V): Visa reported another impressive quarter highlighted by robust 12% organic growth on healthy drivers including U.S. volume accelerating 2ppts to 10% growth (the fastest rate since late 2018, excluding COVID) and cross border accelerating to 13% growth. While this momentum was partially supported by one-offs like the World Cup, tax refunds and fuel prices, headline results also overcame headwinds like tough currency volatility and incentive comps (link).
NUE (\$0.8M sold on 7/28, -0.4z, Figure 34Retail Imbncei NUE): Nucor delivered a strong quarter, beating expectations on earnings and profitability, led by outperformance in its Steel Mills and Raw Materials segments. Results benefited from higher shipments, better margins, and a one-time tariff refund, with utilization running above peers and backlog continuing to build. Downstream operations also contributed through stronger volumes and steady pricing, while construction-related demand drivers (including infrastructure and data centers) remained a key support. Raw Materials improved on higher shipments and better transfer pricing dynamics. The company generated solid free cash flow, used it to fund aggressive buybacks, and the stock rose \~7% on the constructive outlook (link).
INTC (\$5.2M sold on 7/24, -0.3z, Figure 36Retail Imbncei INTC): Intel’s 2Q results and 3Q guidance cleared expectations by wide margins, reflecting supply unlock (yields, cycle times, wafer starts), record DCAI/server momentum, and firm pricing and mix, but a step-function capex cycle that puts a potential equity/debt raise on the table, memory-driven erosion of the client TAM beginning in 2H26, and an external foundry business still lacking an anchor customer keep our analysts UW even as they materially raise estimates (link). The stock was down \~8% post-earnings.
• RTX (\$3.5M sold on 7/24, -0.5z, Figure 38Retail Imbncei RTX): Investors seemed pleased with RTX’s strong operating performance in 2Q as the stock outperformed the S&P 8.5% by on earnings day. Defense and aftermarket were especially strong and while Pratt mix debates will likely remain unsettled. Longer term margin expectations for 19-20% at Collins are unchanged and given the growth and incrementals required, this seems achievable at decade end. And of course, among the defense “primes”, Raytheon performance remains quite strong in both absolute and relative terms (link).

DLR (\$12.3M sold on 7/24, -6.0z, Figure 40Retail Imbncei DLR): Digital Realty Trust was up +11% after reporting strong 2Q results and raising 2026 guidance for total revenue, adj. EBITDA and core FFO, primarly driven by a robust pricing environment. Subsequent to quarter end, the company signed two leases with hyperscale tenants for \$205M of annualized GAAP rent (\$410M at 100% share), which was excluded from the reported 2Q26 backlog (link).
TMUS (\$2.1M sold on 7/23, -0.3z, Figure 42Retail Imbncei TMUS): T-Mobile pulled back \~11% on 2Q results, which likely reflected positioning into the print, which anticipated a beat-and-raise. While our analysts trimmed their 2026 service revenue and EBITDA estimates marginally on forward commentary from the call, their long-term estimates remain largely unchanged, supporting an \~8% core EBITDA and \~11% FCF/share CAGR through 2028E, above peers (link).
CSX (\$1.6M bought on 7/22, 1.1z, Figure 44Retail Imbncei CSX): CSX proved why sentiment was skewed positive heading into the print with another operating beat and raise, despite service metrics which continued to slip throughout the quarter (link). The stock was up +6% post-earnings.
ROL (\$1.7M sold on 7/22, -1.8z, Figure 46Retail Imbncei ROL): Rollins posted a soft 2Q, with the company missing Street expectations across segments. The shortfall versus management’s plan was most pronounced in Residential brands tied to consumer‑initiated demand (search, digital media, inbound calls) as lead volumes softened. Commercial and Termite/Ancillary still showed momentum but came in below expectations. Compounding the demand softness, costs were positioned for a stronger peak season that failed to materialize, driving roughly 120 bps of YoY margin contraction (link). The stock fell \~9%.
Macro & Fundamental Stories
SPCX (\$81.2M bought on 7/24, 1.0z, Figure 48Retail Imbncei SPCX): SpaceX undertook a successful 13th Starship test launch. This was also the second V3 test launch. The rocket achieved its objectives, including deploying 20 Starlink satellites. Importantly, the upper stage landing in the Indian Ocean was relatively soft and controlled, though the booster landing in the Gulf was harder than expected, as not all engines lit for the return to Earth. After the launch, Elon Musk indicated that unless issues emerged from the flight 13 mission data, SpaceX would attempt to catch the second stage in its Mechazilla “chopstick arms” on flight 14. This is a key milestone planned for this year (link). The stock has continued to underperform, reaching a level \~15%+ below its IPO price.
